Run & Bun AI Debug

Gen 8 decision policy (+ documented Run & Bun overlays) over node server.js. This panel is a thin HTTP client: scores and transitions come from /ai/evaluate-actions, /ai/choose-action, and derive/apply/advance — it does not reimplement battle logic. The multi-gen damage controls above remain the calculator oracle. Use Sets / Bridge to build state from calc panels.

Modeled slice, not a full sim. Choose / derive / apply / advance cover the documented AI policy and common move transitions. Residual ordering edge cases, uncommon accuracy interactions, and unmodeled Showdown events stay caller-owned (external engine or you). Gaps are intentional — this is not a complete Pokémon Showdown battle simulator.

Battle Lab

Practice-vs-policy surface for Gen 8 Singles and Doubles. Thin client over the same AI HTTP as Debug: /ai/evaluate-actions, /ai/choose-action, /ai/derive-resolution, /ai/apply-action, /ai/advance-turn, /ai/validate-battle-state. The browser holds display state only — it does not invent mechanics. Field layout follows BattleState.mode; Doubles targeting filters legal actorId/targetIds rows from evaluate (no browser legality engine). Click a same-side active card or use Actor to focus one Pokémon; picked actions highlight targets on the field. Modeled slice: choose / derive / apply / advance-turn residuals & timers. External: unmodeled residual order, accuracy edge cases, and live game events stay caller-owned and are not faked here.

Fight Lab

Pick the trainer you are about to fight, enter the team you are bringing, and see what the Run & Bun AI is expected to do. Fights come from the authored run map in playthrough order. Scores come from the AI policy; a narrow margin means the opponent's move is close to a coin flip and the plan has to survive both. This is a thin client over /planner/* — start the local server first.
